about: Daily feed for the Damus News dashboard. The scheduled daily update appends to events, changes, forecasts, forecast_updates and runs. seed_events and seed_forecasts are a read-only index of the baseline ledger built into the page.

runs.summary: Upload review of the 11-18 recording. Established: the GAO report on AI platforms and attack-planning information, the Aer Lingus diversion, and the wider wave of hoax bomb threats across Europe. Not established: that AI-written code is behind the US outages, which stays a theory. Watch for more hoax-driven diversions over the holidays and for root-cause reports on the outages.
runs.threat_note: Steady. The new items are a capability finding and hoaxes with no explosives, not new attacks.

events.title: GAO: covert tests got Claude, Grok, ChatGPT and Gemini to produce attack-planning information
events.summary: In spring 2026 tests of the four most-used AI platforms, investigators got past initial refusals and obtained feasible attack information from each in under 12 hours. Two produced plans for an explosive device; two produced plans against the electrical grid. Sen. Maggie Hassan plans a Senate hearing in January.
events.note: A finding about capability, not evidence of an attack or plot. The tests used spring 2026 model versions. The companies say safeguards have changed since; OpenAI says the report does not always separate model output from investigators' own input. The clip's mention of hearings today does not match reporting, which puts the hearing in January.

events.title: Hoax bomb threat diverts Aer Lingus EI402 to a French air base under fighter escort
events.summary: The Dublin to Rome Airbus with 157 aboard landed safely at Évreux-Fauville. No explosives were found. The Évreux prosecutor is investigating the pilot's reported initial refusal to land at the military base; Aer Lingus says its crew acted impeccably. The flight recorder is to be examined.
events.note: The clip's flight-path figures (82 minutes aloft, 768 km flown, a pass directly over the base) come from one video's reading of public tracking data and are not independently confirmed.

events.title: Wave of hoax bomb threats hits more than 50 European flights, plus broadcasters and schools
events.summary: From 2 to 6 Nov about 15 airlines received threats against more than 50 flights, with fighter escorts and diversions in several countries. Reuters counts more than 8,000 hoax threats to European schools and airports in a month. No explosives have been found.
events.note: Emails were signed in the name of Male State, a banned Russian far-right group. Its founder denies involvement and the sender is unidentified. Who is behind the wave, and why, is open.

events.title: Theory: AI-written code clashing with legacy systems is behind many of the outages
events.summary: A commentator in the 18 Nov recording says she is hearing that AI-generated code layered over old systems is causing incidents, alongside ordinary causes such as the FAA router change. She calls the overall picture mundane rather than an attack.
events.note: No published root cause for the November outages names AI-written code. Industry surveys do report production incidents from AI-generated code in general. Evidence that would change this: a vendor or agency root-cause report naming AI-written changes.

events.title: DHS secretary faces House questions on outages; CISA staffing and leadership under scrutiny
events.summary: CISA has lost staff in federal workforce cuts and has had no Senate-confirmed director since early 2025. Critics tie the outage response to those cuts; the DHS secretary says he is 98% certain the problems were not cyberattacks.
events.note: The staffing losses are documented. A causal link between the cuts and any specific outage is argued by critics and has not been established.

changes.note: DHS Secretary Mullin said he is 98% certain the recent problems were not cyberattacks, and each affected organisation has published a separate cause.

forecasts.q: A hoax bomb threat forces another fighter-escorted diversion of a passenger flight in Europe by 15 Dec 2026
forecasts.up: New threat emails naming specific flights; holiday travel peak
forecasts.down: Arrests or a takedown of the sending accounts; airlines stop diverting for emailed threats

forecasts.q: The Senate Homeland Security Committee holds a hearing on AI safety by 28 Feb 2027
forecasts.up: Hearing date announced; company witnesses named
forecasts.down: Committee calendar taken over by the Iran war or the outages

forecast_updates.note: The DHS secretary put the odds of a cyberattack near 2% and each outage now has its own stated cause.
